mainTopic: רבן גמליאל in אפרודיטי's bathhouse: his answers to פרוקלוס, and whether they were 'stolen' (misleading)
overview: The משנה tells how a non-Jew named פרוקלוס asked רבן גמליאל how he could bathe in a bathhouse with a statue of אפרודיטי, since the תורה forbids benefiting from עבודה זרה. Outside the bathhouse, רבן גמליאל gave his answers: the bathhouse came first, the statue is only decoration for it, and people urinate in front of this statue, so it is not treated as 'their gods.' The גמרא first asks how he could say even 'one may not answer in the bathhouse' while inside, since תורה is forbidden there in any language. It answers that he said it only after he left. Then רבי אושעיא calls רבן גמליאל's reply a 'stolen' (misleading) answer, and רב חמא בר יוסף says it was honest. Different אמוראים point to different parts as the misleading one: the urinating (רבי אושעיא and רב שימי בר חייא), who came first (אביי), and which serves which (רבה בר עולא). Each time, רב חמא בר יוסף defends רבן גמליאל with a real distinction: worship versus disrespect, a great man's visit counting as favor, permanent versus passing disgrace, and the idol's adornment being forbidden.

steps.title: פרוקלוס asks why רבן גמליאל bathes in אפרודיטי's bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: פרוקלוס quotes the תורה's ban on benefiting from forbidden idol items and asks רבן גמליאל how he can bathe in a bathhouse that has a statue of אפרודיטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: פרוקלוס בן פלוספוס asked רבן גמליאל in עכו, while he was bathing in the bathhouse of אפרודיטי. He said to him: It is written in your תורה, 'Nothing of the banned items shall cling to your hand.' So why are you bathing in the bathhouse of אפרודיטי?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a story: a non-Jew challenges רבן גמליאל for using a bathhouse that has an idol statue in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids getting any benefit from עבודה זרה. פרוקלוס sees רבן גמליאל enjoying a bathhouse decorated with a statue of a Greek goddess, and asks how that is allowed. This question sets up the whole משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (marks the start of the משנה text)
Banned or forbidden items, here meaning idol items
Shall not cling to your hand: do not keep or benefit from it

phrases.english: MISHNA
Proclus ben Plospus asked
Rabban Gamliel in Akko
when he was bathing in the bathhouse of Aphrodite
He said to him: It is written in your Torah
"Nothing of the banned items shall cling to your hand"
For what reason do you bathe
in the bathhouse of Aphrodite?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל פְּרוֹקְלוּס בֶּן פְּלוֹסְפוּס אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is it allowed to bathe in a bathhouse that has an idol statue, given the ban on benefiting from עבודה זרה?

steps.title: רבן גמליאל refuses to answer inside the bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says that one may not answer תורה questions in a bathhouse, so he holds off on answering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: One does not answer in the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל does not answer yet. He explains that speaking words of תורה in a bathhouse is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bathhouse is not a respectful place for תורה, so he holds off on the real answer until he leaves. This one line will become the target of the גמרא's question later.

phrases.english: He said to him: One does not answer in the bathhouse

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין מְשִׁיבִין בַּמֶּרְחָץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Holds off on answering the question from Step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is given yet, because one may not discuss תורה in a bathhouse.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא's first question on this משנה is about this exact line.

steps.title: First answer: the bathhouse came first, and the statue is just decoration
steps.stepSummary: Outside the bathhouse, רבן גמליאל answers that the statue entered his space, not the other way around, and that the statue only decorates the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he left, he said to him: I did not come into its territory; it came into my territory. People don't say, 'Let's make a bathhouse as a decoration for אפרודיטי.' Rather they say, 'Let's make an אפרודיטי as a decoration for the bathhouse.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that he is outside, רבן גמליאל gives his first answer: the bathhouse is the main thing, and the statue is only an extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He makes two points. First, the bathhouse was there before the statue, so he is not entering an idol's place; the statue came into a regular bathhouse. Second, people put up the statue to make the bathhouse look nice, not the other way around, so the building is not a house of עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: And when he left, he said to him
I did not come into its territory
it came into my territory
People do not say: Let us make a bathhouse
as a decoration for Aphrodite
rather, one says: Let us make an Aphrodite
as a decoration for the bathhouse

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁיָּצָא אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי לֹא בָּאתִי בִּגְבוּלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer that was held off in Step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bathhouse is the main thing and came first; the statue is only a decoration for it, so using the bathhouse is not benefiting from עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Second answer: a statue treated with disrespect is not 'their gods'
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל adds that people stand naked and urinate in front of this statue, which nobody would do before a real god. The תורה forbids only 'their gods,' meaning what is treated as a god.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another answer: Even if they gave you a lot of money, you would not go before your idol naked, or after a seminal emission, or urinate in front of it. But this statue stands at the mouth of the drain, and all the people urinate in front of it. The verse only says 'their gods': what people treat as a god is forbidden, and what people do not treat as a god is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives a second, separate answer: this statue is not being worshipped, so it is not forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one would treat a god they worship with such disrespect, not even for a lot of money. Since everyone urinates in front of this statue, it is clearly not being treated as a god. From the word 'אלהיהם' (their gods) we learn that the ban only covers an image that people actually treat as a god.

keyTerms.meaning: One who had a seminal emission (and comes to the bathhouse to purify himself)

steps.whatToRemember: An idol image that people openly treat with disrespect is not 'their gods,' so it is permitted. Only what is treated as a god is forbidden.

phrases.english: Another answer
Even if they gave you a lot of money

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה נִכְנָס לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלְּךָ
phrases.english: you would not go before your idol
naked, or after a seminal emission
or urinate in front of it
This one stands at the mouth of the drain
and all the people urinate in front of it
The verse only says "their gods"

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֱלוֹהַּ — אָסוּר
phrases.english: what people treat as a god is forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֱלוֹהַּ — מוּתָּר
phrases.english: what people do not treat as a god is permitted

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אִם נוֹתְנִים לְךָ מָמוֹן הַרְבֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer, separate from the one in Step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statue is treated with disrespect, so it is not 'their gods'. Only what is treated as a god is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule: whether an image is forbidden depends on whether people treat it as a god.

steps.title: How could רבן גמליאל speak about Torah in the bathhouse at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even saying 'one may not answer in the bathhouse' is a תורה statement, and רבי יוחנן says you may not even think about תורה in a bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: How could he act this way? But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everywhere it is permitted to think about תורה, except in the bathhouse and the bathroom!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבן גמליאל's words in Step 2. It quotes a rule that you may not even think about תורה in a bathhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling someone 'one may not answer in the bathhouse' is itself teaching a law of the תורה. If even thinking about תורה is forbidden in a bathhouse, saying this out loud should be forbidden too. Step 7 gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And how could he act this way?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the answers he gave outside. It is only about the short line 'one may not answer in the bathhouse,' which he said while still inside.

phrases.english: GEMARA
And how could he act this way?
But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say
that Rabbi Yochanan said
Everywhere it is permitted to think
phrases.notes: He means thinking about words of תורה.

phrases.english: except in the bathhouse and the bathroom!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to Step 2 and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's statement 'אין משיבין במרחץ', said inside the bathhouse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If thinking about תורה is forbidden in a bathhouse, then saying a law of the תורה (even this one) out loud there should also be forbidden.

steps.title: Speaking in a secular language does not help
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible defense: maybe רבן גמליאל spoke in a non-holy language. אביי's rule shows that holy matters are forbidden in a bathhouse in any language.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say he said it in a secular language, didn't אביי say that secular matters may be said in the holy language, but holy matters may not be said even in a secular language?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its challenge from Step 5 stronger. It shuts down an easy way out before anyone can use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the problem is only Hebrew, the holy language. אביי teaches that what counts is the content, not the language. So a תורה ruling is forbidden in a bathhouse even when said in another language, and the question against רבן גמליאל stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (the גמרא raises a possible answer in order to reject it)
But didn't he say? (introduces a source that contradicts)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides of אביי's rule. Everyday talk is fine even in Hebrew, but תורה talk is forbidden even in another language. The topic decides, not the language.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: בִּלְשׁוֹן חוֹל אֲמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And if you would say: he said it to him in a secular language,
but didn't Abaye say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁל חוֹל מוּתָּר לְאוֹמְרָן בִּלְשׁוֹן קֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: secular matters may be said in the holy language,
phrases.notes: He means in a bathhouse or bathroom. The גמרא takes that place for granted.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ אָסוּר לְאוֹמְרָן בִּלְשׁוֹן חוֹל!
phrases.english: holy matters may not be said even in a secular language!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: בִּלְשׁוֹן חוֹל אֲמַר לֵיהּ, וְהָאָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge in Step 5 by rejecting a possible defense ahead of time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבן גמליאל could say 'one may not answer in the bathhouse' while still inside the bathhouse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even a secular language would not help, because אביי rules that holy content is forbidden in a bathhouse in any language.

steps.title: He said it only after leaving the bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה's wording differently: רבן גמליאל said 'one may not answer in the bathhouse' only once he had left.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: when he left, he said to him: one may not answer in the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Steps 5 and 6. רבן גמליאל stayed completely silent inside and explained himself only outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that even saying 'one may not answer here' is a תורה statement. The answer moves that sentence to outside the bathhouse. So inside, רבן גמליאל said nothing at all, and nothing was broken.
steps.whatToRemember: In a bathhouse you may not speak about תורה at all, in any language, not even to say that it is forbidden. רבן גמליאל kept silent and explained only once he was outside.

phrases.english: It was taught: when he left,
he said to him: one may not answer in the bathhouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁיָּצָא, אָמַר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised in Steps 5 and 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the משנה's wording so the statement was made outside.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל said 'one may not answer in the bathhouse' while still inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was silent inside and said it only after leaving.

steps.title: Was רבן גמליאל's answer misleading?
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר יוסף quotes רבי אושעיא, who says רבן גמליאל gave the officer a 'stolen', sidestepping answer. רב חמא himself says it was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר יוסף the distinguished said in the name of רבי אושעיא: רבן גמליאל gave that officer a stolen answer. And I say: it is not stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about whether רבן גמליאל's answer to פרוקלוס was honest. Two אמוראים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'stolen' answer is one that sends off the questioner with an argument that sounds convincing but does not really hold up. רבי אושעיא says רבן גמליאל did that, and רב חמא says the answer was truly correct. The next steps explain what was 'stolen' about it.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'stolen' answer: misleading or sidestepping, convincing on the surface but not really true
And I say (the speaker gives his own differing view)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Stolen' here does not mean רבן גמליאל took anything. It means the answer slipped past the real issue.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר יוֹסֵף בְּרַבִּי,
phrases.english: Rav Chama bar Yosef the distinguished said,
phrases.notes: בְּרַבִּי is a title of honor for a respected scholar, not part of his father's name.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Oshaya said:
A stolen answer he gave him,
Rabban Gamliel, to that officer,
phrases.notes: The officer is פרוקלוס, who asked the question in Step 1.

phrases.english: And I say: it is not stolen.
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב חמא himself, disagreeing with the teacher he just quoted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר יוֹסֵף בְּרַבִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: תְּשׁוּבָה גְּנוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the bathhouse speech issue to judging the content of רבן גמליאל's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אושעיא: רבן גמליאל's answer was misleading. רב חמא: it was a true answer.

steps.title: What was misleading about it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of רבן גמליאל's answer רבי אושעיא considered 'stolen'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was its 'stolen' part?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next step. The גמרא wants to know which part of the answer רבי אושעיא was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל gave several arguments in Steps 3 and 4. The גמרא asks which one רבי אושעיא found weak.

phrases.english: What was its 'stolen' part?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה גְּנוּבְתַּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of רבי אושעיא's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of רבן גמליאל's arguments was the misleading one.

steps.title: The argument about urinating before the statue
steps.stepSummary: The misleading part is רבן גמליאל's claim that the statue stands at the drain and everyone urinates in front of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That he said to him: this statue stands at the opening of the drain, and everyone urinates in front of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the exact argument רבי אושעיא meant. It is the argument from Step 4 about people treating the statue with disrespect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל argued that since people disgrace the statue, it clearly is not treated as a god. רבי אושעיא's complaint is aimed at this argument in particular.

phrases.english: That he said to him:
This one stands at the opening of the drain,
and every person urinates in front of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָאָמַר לוֹ: זוֹ עוֹמֶדֶת עַל פִּי הַבִּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'stolen' part was the argument that people urinate in front of the statue.

steps.title: פעור shows disgrace does not cancel an idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why this argument is weak. רבא points out that people relieve themselves before the idol פעור every day, and it is still an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if one urinates in front of it, so what? Didn't רבא say: let פעור prove it, for people relieve themselves before it every day, and it is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי אושעיא is right to call the argument misleading. It brings the example of פעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's argument assumed that a disgraced statue cannot be an idol. But פעור is worshipped by relieving oneself in front of it, and it stays an idol. So acts of disgrace do not prove that a statue is not an idol, and the argument sounds good but does not truly work.

keyTerms.meaning: So what? What difference does it make?
An idol whose worship was done by relieving oneself before it
Cancelled; loses its status as an idol

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא calls רבן גמליאל's answer misleading because disgrace alone does not take away a statue's idol status. פעור is disgraced daily and is still an idol.

phrases.english: And if one urinates in front of it, so what?
But didn't Rava say: let Peor prove it,
for they relieve themselves before it every day,
and it is not cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מַשְׁתִּין בְּפָנֶיהָ מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא: פְּעוֹר יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the argument identified in Step 10 is misleading.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אושעיא's claim that רבן גמליאל's answer was 'stolen'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's statement that פעור, disgraced daily, stays an idol.

steps.title: רב חמא rejects the proof from פעור
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר יוסף says the answer was not misleading. פעור is worshipped by relieving oneself, but אפרודיטי is not, so urinating before her shows disrespect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say it is not a stolen answer. That idol is worshipped that way, but this one is not worshipped that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר יוסף pushes back on רבא's proof from פעור. He says the two idols cannot be compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא argued that people relieve themselves before פעור, and it is still an idol. רב חמא answers that relieving oneself is how פעור is worshipped, so it shows no disrespect there. With אפרודיטי, the same act is real disrespect, so רבן גמליאל's point was honest.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Stolen': a misleading answer that sidesteps the real issue
This is how it is worshipped
And I say: the speaker giving his own view

phrases.english: And I say: it is not a stolen answer,
phrases.notes: This is רב חמא בר יוסף speaking for himself, as in step 8.

phrases.english: that one, its worship is in this way,
and this one, its worship is not in this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ גְּנוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from פעור in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between פעור and אפרודיטי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For פעור, relieving oneself is worship. For אפרודיטי it is disrespect, so the cases are different.

steps.title: אביי locates the misleading part elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the misleading part was רבן גמליאל's claim: 'I did not come into its area; it came into mine.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The stolen part is from here, where he told him: I did not come into its area, it came into my area.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different idea about which part of רבן גמליאל's answer was misleading. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the misleading part was said to be the urinating argument. אביי moves it to the argument about who came first, the bathhouse or the statue.

phrases.english: Abaye said: its stolen part is from here,
where he said to him:
I did not come into its area,
rather it came into my area.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: גְּנוּבְתַּהּ מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new answer to step 9's question, after רבי אושעיא's version was weakened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The misleading part was the claim that the statue came into רבן גמליאל's area.

steps.title: Proof: even an idol's own bathhouse may be used
steps.stepSummary: Even if the bathhouse belonged to the idol, a משנה allows using it as long as one gives the idol no favor. So 'who came first' did not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had come into its area, so what? We learned: An idol that has a bathhouse or garden, one may benefit from them without favor, but not with favor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves why אביי calls this argument misleading. A משנה shows that who came first never mattered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows using an idol's bathhouse or garden as long as you give no thanks or payment to the idol. So even if רבן גמליאל had entered the idol's area, bathing would still be allowed. His 'it came into my area' argument sidestepped the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: So what? What difference does it make?
With favor: giving thanks or payment to the idol's priests

phrases.english: And if he had come into its area, what of it?
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ מֶרְחָץ אוֹ גִינָּה —
phrases.english: An idol that has a bathhouse or a garden —
one may benefit from them without favor,
but one may not benefit from them with favor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בָּא בִּגְבוּלָהּ מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's claim from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That 'it came into my area' was a sidestepping argument
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about an idol's bathhouse or garden

steps.title: רב חמא: for רבן גמליאל, no favor is still favor
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר יוסף says it was not misleading. When someone as important as רבן גמליאל visits, it is like others showing favor, so the 'who came first' point mattered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say it is not stolen. For רבן גמליאל, even without favor counts like others giving favor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר יוסף rejects אביי's idea. He says the 'who came first' argument was actually needed for someone like רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's permission works for an ordinary person who gives no favor. But a visit from רבן גמליאל honors the place by itself, like favor from others. So he needed the extra point that the statue came into his area.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like favor shown by others

phrases.english: And I say: it is not a stolen answer,
for Rabban Gamliel's 'without favor'
is like the favor of others.
phrases.notes: Just his presence honors the place, even if he pays and thanks no one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ גְּנוּבָה, שֶׁלֹּא בְּטוֹבַת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof from step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using the משנה to show the 'who came first' argument was pointless
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's permission does not fully cover a great person like רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: רב שימי בר חייא: the drain claim was misleading
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא says the misleading part was 'it stands at the drain and everyone urinates in front of it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא said: The stolen part is from here, where he told him: This stands at the drain, and everyone urinates in front of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר חייא gives his view of which part was misleading. This sets up his own proof, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He picks the same part as in step 10, the urinating argument. But he will bring a new proof from a משנה instead of רבא's proof from פעור, which רב חמא rejected.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Chiya said:
its stolen part is from here,
where he said to him:
this stands at the drain
and all people urinate in front of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר: גְּנוּבְתַּהּ מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the urinating argument from step 10, after אביי's approach was rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The misleading part was the claim that people urinate in front of the statue.

steps.title: Proof: disrespect does not cancel an idol
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that spitting, urinating, dragging, or throwing filth at an idol does not cancel its status. So the urinating argument proved nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they urinate in front of it, so what? We learned: If he spat in front of it, urinated in front of it, dragged it, or threw filth at it, it is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב שימי's point with a משנה. Disrespect toward an idol does not stop it from being an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל suggested that urinating before the statue showed it was not treated as a god. The משנה says such acts never cancel an idol. So that argument sidestepped the real reason, which makes it 'stolen.'

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelled: no longer counts as an idol

steps.whatToRemember: רב שימי בר חייא points to the same urinating argument as רבי אושעיא, but proves his point from a משנה about disrespecting an idol instead of from פעור.

phrases.english: And if they urinate in front of it, what of it?
But didn't we learn:
If he spat in front of it, urinated in front of it,
dragged it, or threw filth at it —
it is not cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מַשְׁתִּינִין בְּפָנֶיהָ מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב שימי's claim from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the urinating argument was a sidestepping answer
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that disrespect does not cancel an idol

steps.title: A passing insult is different from permanent disgrace
steps.stepSummary: The urination argument was not misleading. The משנה deals with someone who insults an idol for a moment and later makes up with it. Here the statue sits in disgrace all the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say: it is not misleading. There, in the משנה, a person rages at the idol for a moment and then goes back and makes up with it. Here, every single hour the statue stands in disgrace.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר יוסף pushes back on רב שימי בר חייא's proof in step 17 and says the urination point really was a good argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about spitting or urinating at an idol talks about a one-time outburst of anger, which does not end the worship. A statue placed at a drain, where people urinate in front of it all day, shows that nobody treats it as a god at all. So רבן גמליאל's argument was honest.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not misleading (not a 'stolen,' tricky answer)

phrases.english: And I say: it is not misleading.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — לְפִי שַׁעְתָּא הוּא רָתַח עֲלַהּ,
phrases.english: There, he only rages against it for the moment,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה about spitting and urinating at an idol from the last step.

phrases.english: and afterward he goes back and appeases it.
Here, every single hour,
it stands in its disgrace.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ גְּנוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה in step 17 by drawing a distinction between the cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב שימי בר חייא's claim that the urination argument was misleading.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with a one-time angry insult, not a permanent state of disgrace like a statue placed by a drain.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: the misleading part was 'the statue adorns the bathhouse'
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא says the misleading part was רבן גמליאל's claim that people make אפרודיטי an adornment for the bathhouse, not the bathhouse an adornment for אפרודיטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: The misleading part comes from here, where he said to him: People do not say, 'Let us make a bathhouse as an adornment for אפרודיטי.' Rather, they say, 'Let us make אפרודיטי as an adornment for the bathhouse.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new suggestion is offered for which part of רבן גמליאל's answer was misleading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל argued that the bathhouse is the main thing and the statue is just decoration. רבה בר עולא says this point is the misleading one. The next step will explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Aphrodite, the Greek goddess whose statue stood in the bathhouse

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
Its misleading part is from here, where he said to him:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן גמליאל, answering the man who questioned him in the bathhouse.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִין: נַעֲשָׂה מֶרְחָץ נוֹי לְאַפְרוֹדִיטֵי,
phrases.english: People do not say: Let us make a bathhouse as an adornment for Aphrodite,
rather: Let us make Aphrodite as an adornment for the bathhouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's and רב שימי בר חייא's suggestions were defended, a third candidate for the misleading part is offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The misleading part of רבן גמליאל's answer was the claim that the statue serves the bathhouse, not the other way around.

steps.title: Words alone cannot make an object forbidden for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: Even if people did say the bathhouse was made for אפרודיטי, it would not matter. A ברייתא teaches that declaring a house or cup 'for עבודה זרה' does nothing, because there is no הקדש for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if people did say, 'Let us make a bathhouse as an adornment for אפרודיטי,' what of it? But a ברייתא teaches: Someone who says, 'This house is for עבודה זרה,' or 'This cup is for עבודה זרה,' has said nothing, because there is no הקדש for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves why רבה בר עולא called that point misleading: the words people say would not make the bathhouse forbidden anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object can be made holy for the בית המקדש just by saying so (הקדש). For עבודה זרה there is no such power of words. So whether people 'call' the bathhouse an adornment for אפרודיטי changes nothing, and רבן גמליאל's argument answered a question that did not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?
He has said nothing; his words have no effect
Making something holy by declaring it

phrases.english: And if people did say: 'Let us make a bathhouse as an adornment for Aphrodite,'
what of it?
But isn't it taught: One who says, 'This house is for idol worship,'

phrases.aramaic: ״כּוֹס זֶה לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה״ — לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: or 'This cup is for idol worship,' has said nothing,
because there is no consecration for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אָמַר ״נַעֲשָׂה מֶרְחָץ לְאַפְרוֹדִיטֵי נוֹי״ מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה בר עולא's claim in step 19 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'bathhouse versus adornment' argument was irrelevant and therefore misleading.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: declaring a house or cup 'for idol worship' has no effect, since there is no הקדש for idol worship.

steps.title: Not forbidden by words, but still an adornment of the idol
steps.stepSummary: This point was not misleading either. Even if words cannot make the bathhouse forbidden, it would still be an adornment (נוי) of the idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I say: it is not misleading. Granted that the bathhouse would not become forbidden by words, but at least it would be an adornment of the idol.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר יוסף rejects רבה בר עולא's suggestion and defends רבן גמליאל's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only shows that words cannot make the bathhouse itself into a forbidden idol object. But if the bathhouse really served as decoration for אפרודיטי, it would have the status of the idol's נוי, and that is also forbidden. So the question of which one serves which really mattered.
steps.whatToRemember: Three parts of רבן גמליאל's answer were suggested as 'misleading': the urinating (רבי אושעיא and רב שימי בר חייא), who came first (אביי), and which serves which (רבה בר עולא). רב חמא בר יוסף defended each one: פעור is worshipped that way but אפרודיטי is not; a great man's visit counts as favor; this disgrace is permanent; and the idol's adornment is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two different issues: the bathhouse becoming a forbidden idol object by words (which cannot happen) and the bathhouse counting as the idol's adornment (which can happen).

phrases.english: And I say: it is not misleading.
Granted that it does not become forbidden,
there is at least the status of adornment.
phrases.notes: He means an adornment of an idol, which is also forbidden to benefit from.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ גְּנוּבָה, נְהִי דְּאִיתְּסוֹרֵי לָא מִיתַּסְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 20 and with it רבה בר עולא's suggestion in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבה בר עולא's claim that the 'adornment' argument was misleading.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא only rules out the bathhouse becoming forbidden by words. It ignores that a bathhouse serving the idol would count as its forbidden adornment.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows there are different ways an object can be forbidden because of an idol. It can be forbidden as the idol object itself, or as the idol's adornment, and the second way does not depend on spoken words.
